gap: None of the results ChatGPT got say that Toybox's cheapest new Alpha Four bundle, the $199 'Pro Saver', costs $50 less than the $249 Starter bundle (both come with one Printer Food) only because it signs the buyer up for Toybox Pro. Toybox's store lists Toybox Pro at $20. The store says the membership starts 30 days after purchase (or when it's linked to an account) and keeps charging 'until you cancel'.
standout_why: I compared against itechguides.com, which ChatGPT got as result 3 and which gives no Toybox price or filament cost, and 3dprinterlab.org (result 5). 3dprinterlab says 'some bundles depend on a paid Toybox Pro membership' and gives the Pro Saver price as $249, which is wrong today ($199). It says nothing about auto-renewal or the $20 charge, and gives no Printer Food price. I couldn't load the Tom's Hardware page that ChatGPT cited: the fetch returned only menus, and a direct download needed permission I didn't have. So I can't rule out that it covers this. ChatGPT's own card priced Toybox at $249–$375, but no new Alpha Four bundle on toybox.com costs more than $299.
decides: This keeps Toybox Alpha Four as the pick for ages 5–8 and changes how to buy it. Either get the $249 Starter, which has no subscription, or get the $199 Pro Saver and cancel Toybox Pro within 30 days. Also, our page's 'filament about $60/kg' figure is out of date: Printer Food now costs $15 per 500 g, about $30/kg. That removes most of Toybox's running-cost penalty against standard PLA. For an enclosed printer, Flashforge's own store sells the Adventurer 5M Pro for $379. The plain Adventurer 5M is $249, but the same store sells a $39.99 enclosure kit for it, so it is not the enclosed option.
